newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index rockets to record close.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index rockets to record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's blue chips ploughed into record territory on Friday as a surge in HSBC Holdings Plc shares propelled the Hang Seng Index to close at an all-time high.
The blue-chip index soared 341.24 points, or 2.37 percent, to close at a record high of 14,757.81. Turnover was a robust HK$18.74 billion compared with HK$16.39 billion on Thursday.
"The market is certainly riding a wave of liquidity," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities. "I think there is a number of covered warrants being issued."
Share prices began a rapid ascent in afternoon trade with investors scrambling to cover short positions, brokers said.
Futures-related activity also boosted the cash market. The June Hang Seng Index contract soared 380 points to 14,860.
"Investors are positive on the market in June," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.
"There is also the Beijing Enterprises money coming back into the market."

Applications for Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd's initial public offering tied up HK$215 billion in the Hong Kong banking system. Unsuccessful applicants got their cheques back on Thursday when the stock made its market debut.
Investors snatched up shares in the red chip for the second day in a row, with Beijing Enterprises finishing Friday up HK$5.00 at HK$45.20. The stock was issued at HK$12.48.
"In the short term it has already touched its target price," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.
"It is difficult to tell where this stock is going because of the liquidity."

Investors also bid up other red chips, with China Resources Enterprise Ltd surging HK$1.05 to HK$27.20, China Merchants Holdings (International) Co Ltd up HK$1.25 at HK$14.10 and China Overseas Land & Investment Ltd adding HK$0.425 to HK$5.35.
Hongkong Telecom gained HK$0.45 to HK$17.15 on continued speculation it would team up with a Chinese partner.
"Telecom is behaving like a red chip," said Gary Wong, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
Shares in HSBC Holdings ended at a record high, up HK$7.00 at HK$235.00.
